# 1) Commit changes and push to default branch (develop)
git checkout develop
git pull origin develop
git add .
git commit -m "Add workflows and populateAuthors fix"
git push origin develop

# 2) Feature branch workflow (create, commit, push)
git checkout -b feature/my-feature
# make changes...
git add .
git commit -m "Work on feature"
git push origin feature/my-feature

# 3) Create & push UAT tag (annotated)
git tag -a uat/2025-10-16 -m "UAT deploy for 2025-10-16"
git push origin uat/2025-10-16

# 4) Create & push Production tag (semantic version)
git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "Release v1.2.3"
git push origin v1.2.3

# OR create & push Production tag (prod/*)
git tag -a prod/2025-10-16 -m "Prod deploy 2025-10-16"
git push origin prod/2025-10-16

# 5) Tag a specific commit (use actual commit SHA)
git tag -a prod/1.2.3 <COMMIT_SHA> -m "Prod deploy for commit <COMMIT_SHA>"
git push origin prod/1.2.3

# 6) Manually trigger workflow via GitHub CLI (workflow_dispatch)
gh workflow run "CI + Tag-based Deployments" --ref develop
# or by filename
gh workflow run main.yml --ref develop

# 7) Inspect runs with GitHub CLI
gh run list
gh run view <run-id> --log

# 8) Re-run or re-deploy a tag (delete remote tag and re-push)
git push --delete origin prod/2025-10-16
git tag -f prod/2025-10-16
git push origin prod/2025-10-16

# Notes:
# - Replace placeholder values (dates, versions, <COMMIT_SHA>, branch names) before running.
# - Use annotated tags (-a) as recommended.
# - Ensure workflows are committed to the default branch (develop) and Actions are enabled.
# - If using gh CLI, authenticate first: gh auth login
